main_issue: How D's wake setup (tent, music) can accommodate neighbours' needs: A's wheelchair path, B's sleep versus music in the evening, C's morning exercise corner.

A-B.evidence: A (turns 1, 3) raised the wheelchair path and B (turns 4, 6, 9) raised music; neither addressed the other's concern.

A-C.evidence: A asked for a path (turns 1, 3) and C asked for a corner (turn 7); the two requests were separate and neither spoke to the other.

A-D.evidence: D agrees to keep a path clear (turn 2); A thanks D and accepts (turn 3); A offers condolences again at the end (turn 32).

B-C.evidence: B (music, turns 4-9) and C (morning exercise corner, turn 7) never addressed each other.

B-D.evidence: B wanted no music 7-10pm (turn 9) and D refused (turn 13). D then proposed far-side speakers kept low, a check at 8, and no music on Sunday if it was still too loud. B accepted: 'That's a fair offer' (turn 14), and D confirmed (turn 18).

C-D.evidence: D agrees to keep a corner clear for C's 7am group (turn 8); C closes with 'Take care, Agent D' (turn 29).
